newsitem.title: UK: Kexim to launch $500 million bond shortly - lead.
newsitem.headline: Kexim to launch $500 million bond shortly - lead.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Korea will launch a $500 million five-year Eurobond later today, a spokesman for joint lead manager SBC Warburg said.
"The deal will be launched this afternoon with pricing before noon London time on Tuesday," Patrick O'Brien told bankers at a presentation by Kexim in London.
Nomura International will be joint lead manager.
The deal will be the largest Eurobond, as opposed to global or Yankee bond, issued by a Korean borrower.
O'Brien at SBC Warburg said pricing would be in line with the clearly defined Korean yield curve. Market talk was for a spread in the low 40s basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Kexim launched a $200 million five-year bond in June at a 47 b.p. spread which subsequently tightened to 41 39 b.p. at one stage before widening again slightly, SBC Warburg said. In February, Kexim launched a 10-year Eurodollar bond at a 77 b.p. spread. That has since tightened to the low 60s b.p. on expectations Korea will join the OECD later this year .
SBC Warburg's global head of credit research, Bob Janjuah, said he expected Moody's Investors Service would upgrade Korea oner notch from A1 when its OECD membership was confirmed.
OECD membership would see Kexim's BIS risk weighting fall to at least 20 percent from 100 percent, Janjuah said.
Kexim is state-owned and effectively has a sovereign guarantee.
